title: Some Command Palette extensions remain running even after Powertoys is closed
author: heheeheeha

judgment.rationale: The issue and maintainer edits identify a concrete extension-lifecycle gap: some third-party extensions survive host shutdown, and the newest maintainer comment says extensions may not receive a stop signal when disabled in the Command Palette UI. The SDK-side shutdown contract exists, but host and extension behavior need coordinated verification.
evidence: The report shows extension processes remaining after PowerToys exits.
A maintainer says affected extensions need to adopt an SDK shutdown fix from 2025.
Random Data Generator had a fix submitted.
The newest maintainer comment says Colors behaves correctly but no extension appears to receive a signal when merely disabled in CmdPal UI.
judgment.recommended_action: Split and investigate host-exit versus UI-disable lifecycle signaling, then update affected extensions against the current SDK contract.

fix_assessment.rationale: Public evidence identifies the lifecycle boundary but not whether the remaining defect is in host signaling, extension adoption, or both.

proposed_fixes.title: Unify Command Palette extension stop signaling for disable and host exit
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Extension processes depend on an SDK stop signal, but host exit and UI disable follow different lifecycle paths; some extensions have not adopted the SDK contract and compliant extensions may not receive a signal on disable.
plan: Build a lifecycle matrix for host exit, CmdPal close, and extension disable using compliant and outdated extensions.
Ensure the host sends and awaits the supported stop signal on every operation that promises process shutdown.
Track extension-specific SDK updates separately from host signaling fixes.
verification: Exercise host exit and UI disable with Colors and another known extension while monitoring process lifetime.
Confirm compliant extensions exit within a bounded interval and outdated extensions are identified explicitly.

confidence.rationale: The SDK ownership and two lifecycle paths are public, but the remaining failures have not been separated into host and extension defects.

issue_context.summary: Some Command Palette extension processes survive host shutdown, and UI disable may not signal any extension to stop.
known_information: The SDK has a shutdown-handling update.
At least one extension fix was submitted.
Colors may follow the extension contract yet still survive UI disable.
inferences: Host exit and extension disable are distinct lifecycle paths and should not be conflated.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is ready for a focused lifecycle matrix rather than another generic request to update PowerToys.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the current public issue body, labels, assignees, and up to the latest 20 public comments returned by GitHub.
Kept the existing dashboard read-only; no dashboard files were modified or published.

information_gaps.information: Which current extensions survive full host exit versus only UI disable.
information_gaps.why_needed: The two paths imply different ownership.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Test a small known set on current stable and record process lifetime for both operations.

actions.label: Approve unify command palette extension stop signaling for disable and host exit
actions.note: Approve/start the fork-side design workflow from this public-evidence fix plan. No upstream write occurs from this action.

actions.label: Reproduce Some Command Palette extensions remain running even after Powertoys is closed
actions.note: Maintainer-side reproduction reduces the recorded implementation uncertainty without asking the reporter to perform code investigation.

prerequisites: Current CmdPal with Colors and one additional third-party extension installed.
steps: Launch each extension and record its process.
Disable the extension in CmdPal and check process lifetime.
Re-enable it, then fully exit PowerToys and check again.
reproduce.expected_result: A supported shutdown operation signals compliant extensions and their processes exit.
reproduce.observed_result: Some processes survive host exit, and UI disable may not signal extensions.
